# Test Fixture Provenance

Every committed fixture (GGUF header, quantized block, tokenizer vector, logits snapshot) must have a row here. A fixture without provenance is not acceptable evidence and will be rejected at the gate.

## Required fields

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | Short stable identifier used by tests |
| `path` | Path relative to `tests/fixtures/` |
| `kind` | `gguf-header`, `quant-block`, `tokenizer-vector`, `logits`, `tiny-model` |
| `source` | Upstream project + version/commit (e.g. llama.cpp `@<sha>`) |
| `command` | Exact command that produced the fixture |
| `input_sha256` | Hash of the source model/prompt/input |
| `output_sha256` | Hash of the committed fixture |
| `license` | License of the upstream data and any redistribution constraint |
| `notes` | Scope, tolerance, or known limitation |

## Rules

- Prefer **small** fixtures (≤2 MB each; total ≤10 MB) and text formats.
- Tokenizer vectors must come from llama.cpp (or another independent reference), not from this repository's tokenizer.
- Quantized blocks must be extracted from a real GGUF or generated by the reference implementation, not by `quantize_*_cpu` in this repo.
- Logits snapshots must record model hash, prompt, seed, temperature (normally 0), and the exact comparison tolerance.
- If redistribution is not permitted, commit a **generator script + hashes** instead and document how to regenerate the fixture locally.
- Update this file in the same PR that adds or changes a fixture.

## The references used by Phase 7A-3

Two independent upstreams, pinned:

| reference | pin | what it provides |
|---|---|---|
| `ggml-org/llama.cpp` | `@149f5641b931aaf33697d70f9abc90c3e5300247` (2026-11-03) | the reference **tokenizer** (`llama-tokenize`), the reference **quantizer** (`llama-quantize`), and the reference **NumPy** quant implementation and GGUF reader (`gguf-py`) |
| `openai-community/gpt2` | `@607a30d783dfa663caf39e06633721c8d4cfcd7e` | the GPT-2 byte-level BPE vocabulary (`vocab.json`, `merges.txt`), MIT |
| `ggml-org/models` | `tinyllamas/stories260K.gguf`, `tinyllamas/stories15M.gguf` | the TinyLlama SentencePiece vocabulary and the source model for the quantized blocks, Apache-2.0 |

None of the fixtures was produced by `src/`: the goldens must not depend on the
code they are used to test. In particular there is **no**
`quantize_*_cpu` → `dequantize_*_cpu` pair anywhere in this registry.

The generator is [`make_fixtures.py`](make_fixtures.py). It drives llama.cpp's
own binaries and its own `gguf-py` package; it imports nothing from `src/`.

### Reproducing

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp && cd llama.cpp
git checkout 149f5641b931aaf33697d70f9abc90c3e5300247
cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF -DLLAMA_BUILD_TESTS=OFF \
      -DLLAMA_BUILD_EXAMPLES=OFF -DLLAMA_BUILD_SERVER=OFF
cmake --build build --target llama-tokenize llama-quantize -j

# the upstream inputs
curl -L -o gpt2-vocab.json https://huggingface.co/openai-community/gpt2/resolve/607a30d783dfa663caf39e06633721c8d4cfcd7e/vocab.json
curl -L -o gpt2-merges.txt https://huggingface.co/openai-community/gpt2/resolve/607a30d783dfa663caf39e06633721c8d4cfcd7e/merges.txt
curl -L -o stories260K.gguf https://huggingface.co/ggml-org/models/resolve/main/tinyllamas/stories260K.gguf
curl -L -o stories15M.gguf  https://huggingface.co/ggml-org/models/resolve/main/tinyllamas/stories15M.gguf

cd tests/fixtures
python3 make_fixtures.py tokenizer --llama-cpp /path/to/llama.cpp \
    --gpt2-vocab /path/to/gpt2-vocab.json --gpt2-merges /path/to/gpt2-merges.txt \
    --gpt2-revision 607a30d783dfa663caf39e06633721c8d4cfcd7e \
    --spm-gguf /path/to/stories260K.gguf --spm-revision "ggml-org/models@main:tinyllamas/stories260K.gguf" --out .
python3 make_fixtures.py quant --llama-cpp /path/to/llama.cpp --model /path/to/stories15M.gguf --out .
python3 make_fixtures.py gguf-expectations --gguf tiny_gguf.gguf --out tiny_gguf_expectations.json
```

## Scope and tolerances

- The token-ID goldens are **exact**: the token IDs must match llama.cpp's
  element for element.
- The dequantization goldens are **exact** in FP16: the repository's CPU
  dequantizers and the HIP kernels reproduce the FP16 rounding of llama.cpp's
  FP32 reference values with no tolerance at all.
- The GGUF expectations are **exact** for the metadata, the descriptors and the
  recorded values.
- The golden tests never call this repository's tokenizer, quantizer or parser
  to *derive* an expected value. They only compare against the fixtures.

### A note on `git add`

The repository's `.gitignore` excludes `*.bin` and `*.gguf` — the patterns for
model weights, not for fixtures. The four binary fixtures above are therefore
committed with `git add -f`:

```bash
git add -f tests/fixtures/*.bin tests/fixtures/*.gguf
```

A plain `git add tests/fixtures/` would **silently skip** them, which would
leave the golden tests failing on a fresh clone with no visible cause. The
provenance check (`audit/evidence/G1/7A-3/verify-provenance.py`) compares the
files on disk against this registry, so a fixture that was not committed shows
up as a missing file rather than as a silent gap.
